;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbass]]
**The [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian military]] reports that eight Ukrainian soldiers have been captured by pro-Russian fighters near the village of [[Novotroitske, Donetsk Oblast|Novotroyitske]]. [https://www.newsweek.com/ukraine-russia-peace-conflict-president-1432621 (''Newsweek'')] [https://www.unian.info/war/10558680-eight-ukrainian-soldiers-taken-captive-by-russia-led-forces-in-donbas.html (UNIAN)]
*At least nine people are killed when a [[Car bomb|car bomber]] attacks a police checkpoint in the [[Bondhere District]] of [[Mogadishu]] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/05/killed-mogadishu-car-explosion-190522100407045.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Central African Republic Civil War (2012–present)]]
**A [[France|French]] nun is found decapitated in a village in the [[Central African Republic]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/20190522-central-african-republic-french-spanish-nun-murdered-vatican (France24)]
**Armed [[militia]]s kill over 30 civilians in one of the deadliest attacks since a peace deal was reached back in February of this year. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-centralafrica-security/armed-group-kills-34-civilians-in-central-african-republic-idUSKCN1SS2HN (Reuters)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (April 2019–present)]]
**[[Syria]]n government airstrikes in Syria’s northwestern de-escalation zones target the towns of [[Maarrat al-Nu'man]] and Maarat Herma in [[Idlib Governorate]], killing twelve civilians. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/regime-attacks-kill-12-in-syrias-de-escalation-zones/1484381 (AA)] [https://www.dailysabah.com/politics/2019/05/23/assad-regime-attacks-kill-12-in-de-escalation-zones (''Daily Sabah'')]
**The [[Syrian Army]] and [[Iran]]-back militants shell the town of Khan Sheykhun and the villages of Al-Kassabiyya, Abdin, Karasaa, Kafr Sajna and Al-Naqeer. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/regime-attacks-kill-12-in-syrias-de-escalation-zones/1484381 (AA)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economy of the United Kingdom]]
**[[British Steel Limited]] goes into compulsory liquidation after rescue talks between the [[Government of the United Kingdom|British government]] and the company's owners, [[Greybull Capital]], fail. Around 5,000 workers are employed by the company, 3,800 of whom are based in the UK. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-48365241 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Tornadoes of 2019]]
**A powerful [[tornado]] hits [[Jefferson City, Missouri|Jefferson City]], [[Missouri]], leaving people trapped or injured and structural damage according to city and state officials. At least three people are killed in southwestern Missouri when a storm system sweeps across the state causing extensive damage. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jefferson-city-missouri-tornado-people-trapped-extensive-damage-live-updates-today-2019-05-23/ (CBS News)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/weather/tornado-emergency-issued-near-joplin-anniversary-deadly-storm-n1009101 (NBC News)] [https://www.kansascity.com/news/weather-news/article230733039.html (''The Kansas City Star'')]

;International relations
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**[[United States]] [[Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor|F-22 Raptor]]s intercept four [[Russia]]n [[Tupolev Tu-95|Tu-95]] bombers and two [[Sukhoi Su-35|Su-35]] fighter jets off the coast of [[Alaska]] on Tuesday and Wednesday, according to a statement from the [[North American Aerospace Defense Command]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/us-military-jets-intercepted-russian-bombers-fighter-jets/story?id=63176345 (ABC News)]
*[[Chagos Archipelago sovereignty dispute]]
**The [[United Nations General Assembly]] passes a non-binding resolution demanding the [[United Kingdom]] return control of the [[Chagos Archipelago]] to [[Mauritius]]. The Mauritians claim they were forced to give up the islands to the British in 1965 in exchange for independence. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-48371388 (BBC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[Timeline of investigations into Donald Trump and Russia (2019)]]
**The [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]] agrees to provide the [[United States House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence|House Intelligence Committee]] with  intelligence files from [[Mueller special counsel investigation|special counsel Robert Mueller's investigation]] of [[Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections|Russian interference in the 2016 election]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/politics/in-compromise-justice-department-will-reveal-intelligence-files-from-mueller-probe-to-house-committee/ar-AABJZki?ocid=spartandhp (''USA Today'' via MSN.com)]
*Lawyer [[Michael Avenatti]] is indicted in separate cases charging him with allegedly stealing about $300,000 from [[Stormy Daniels]] and blackmailing [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2019/05/22/michael-avenatti-indicted-for-alleged-extortion-attempt-against-nike.html (CNBC)]
*[[Tax returns of Donald Trump]]
**The [[New York State Legislature]] passes a bill that will authorize state tax officials to release U.S. President [[Donald Trump]]'s state returns to Congress.  [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/05/22/nyregion/trump-state-tax-returns.html (''The New York Times'')]  
**Judge [[Edgardo Ramos]] of the [[United States District Court for the Southern District of New York]] rules [[Deutsche Bank]] and [[Capital One]] can release President Trump's financial records to Congress. [https://www.cnbc.com/2019/05/22/judge-says-deutsche-bank-can-give-trump-financial-records-to-democrats.html (CNBC)] 
;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Indonesian general election]]
** Six people die and more than 200 are injured in the Indonesian capital, [[Jakarta]], after protesters of the announced results of the presidential election clash with security forces and set fire to a police dormitory and vehicles. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/may/22/indonesia-riots-protesters-clash-with-security-forces-over-election-result (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Andrea Leadsom]] resigns as the [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Leader of the House of Commons]] with immediate effect in response to [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Theresa May]]'s handling of [[Brexit]]. Several other cabinet ministers are reportedly threatening to resign. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-48374098 (BBC News)]
